name: Somatrogon

lead: Somatrogon (Ngenla) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved in the US for children aged 3 and older whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone. It comes up in height discussions because GH drives growth velocity and, over time, final height.

It binds the growth hormone receptor, activates STAT5b signalling and raises IGF-1, promoting linear growth. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin in children with a diagnosed deficiency, and reviews describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety to daily GH. No study has tested it for height in children without a deficiency.

paras: It is prescribed by specialists as a weekly injection in place of daily GH for diagnosed growth failure, with growth tracked over months and years of treatment.

The label lists warnings such as neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only and approved for diagnosed deficiency.

angle.text: Somatrogon is a weekly prescription growth hormone that raises growth velocity in children with diagnosed GH deficiency, which is why height-focused people follow it. Trials are in children with deficiency.

lead: Somatrogon (MOD-4023; brand name Ngenla) is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analogue given by subcutaneous injection once a week. In the United States it is indicated for children aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone [1][2].

In phase 3 trials, weekly somatrogon was compared with daily somatropin in prepubertal children with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), including a 12-month open-label randomised study and a study in Japanese children [3][4]. Reviews of the three long-acting growth hormones (lonapegsomatropin, somatrogon and somapacitan) describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety profiles to daily growth hormone in 52-week trials [5].
It is a prescription medicine for diagnosed deficiency. No study has tested it for height gain in children without a diagnosed deficiency.
infobox: Long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analogue
Pediatric growth failure due to inadequate GH secretion, ages 3+ [1]

paras: The US label indicates somatrogon for pediatric patients aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone [1]. A phase 3 study in children born small for gestational age or with idiopathic short stature is registered and recruiting [6].

According to the label, somatrogon binds the growth hormone receptor and activates the STAT5b signalling pathway, increasing serum IGF-1; GH and IGF-1 then drive metabolic changes and linear growth [1].

The US labels for long-acting growth hormones list warnings including increased mortality in acute critical illness, severe hypersensitivity, increased risk of neoplasms (notably second neoplasms in childhood cancer survivors), glucose intolerance and diabetes mellitus, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism [1]. Label pregnancy information notes that no human data are available, and that rat reproduction studies showed no embryo-fetal toxicity [1].

A 12-month phase 3 trial randomised prepubertal children with GHD to weekly somatrogon or daily somatropin and reported on efficacy and safety [3]; a Japanese phase 3 study in 44 prepubertal children made a similar comparison with daily Genotropin [4][7]. A treatment-burden study compared weekly and daily injections from the patient perspective [8][9]. A five-year open-label extension of a phase 2 dose-finding study has been published [10]. A systematic review and a network meta-analysis compared long-acting with daily growth hormone [11][12].
Post-marketing surveillance in Korea and a special investigation in Japan are registered [13][14].

timeline.event: Phase 3 trial of MOD-4023 in children with GHD starts [15].
